question: Which of the following crop is NOT associated with dryland farming?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dryland farming** refers to agricultural practices in regions with limited rainfall, typically less than 500 mm annually. Crops cultivated under dryland farming are drought-resistant and require minimal water.
 
• **Jute** is not associated with dryland farming because it requires a humid climate with high rainfall (typically above 1500 mm annually) for proper growth. It thrives in regions with adequate water supply and is primarily grown in areas like West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.
 
• **Guar**, also known as cluster bean, is a drought-resistant crop widely grown in arid and semi-arid regions, making it suitable for dryland farming.
 
• **Bajra** (pearl millet) is a staple dryland crop grown in regions with low rainfall. It is heat- and drought-tolerant, making it ideal for dryland farming.
 
• **Ragi** (finger millet) is another dryland crop known for its resilience to drought and ability to grow in poor soils with minimal water requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jute:**

 
 
• **Climate:** Jute requires a warm and humid climate with temperatures between 24°C to 37°C and annual rainfall of 1500-2500 mm.
 
• **Uses:** Jute is primarily used for making ropes, mats, sacks, and other eco-friendly products.
 
• **Major growing regions:** It is cultivated mostly in eastern India, including states like West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and Assam.
 
• **Harvesting:** Jute is harvested during the rainy season, and its cultivation is dependent on adequate water availability.
 
 
 
• **Dryland Farming:**
 
 
• **Definition:** Dryland farming refers to agricultural practices in areas with low rainfall and no irrigation facilities. It relies on moisture conservation techniques.
 
• **Crops:** Common crops include millet (bajra), sorghum, ragi, pulses, and oilseeds such as mustard and groundnut.
 
• **Regions:** Dryland farming is prevalent in arid and semi-arid regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka, and parts of Maharashtra.
 
• **Techniques:** Farmers adopt techniques such as contour plowing, mulching, and planting drought-resistant crop varieties to conserve soil moisture.
 
 
 
• **Guar:**
 
 
• **Scientific name:** Cyamopsis tetragonoloba.
 
• **Uses:** Guar is used in food industries as a thickener and stabilizer. Its gum is also used in oil and gas extraction.
 
• **Location:** Guar is widely grown in Rajasthan and Haryana due to its drought resistance.
 
 
 
• **Bajra:**
 
 
• **Scientific name:** Pennisetum glaucum.
 
• **Uses:** Bajra is rich in nutrients and is used in making various traditional foods such as rotis.
 
• **Location:** It is commonly cultivated in dry regions like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Ragi:**
 
 
• **Scientific name:** Eleusine coracana.
 
• **Uses:** Ragi is a highly nutritious cereal crop used for making porridge, bread, and malt.
 
• **Location:** It thrives in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh, particularly in dry areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dryland farming in India:**

 
 
• It accounts for nearly **40% of the total cultivated area** in India.
 
• Dryland areas contribute significantly to the production of **millets, pulses, and oilseeds**.
 
• Regions such as **Rajasthan**, **Maharashtra**, and parts of **Gujarat** are prominent for dryland agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in dryland farming:**
 
 
• **Water scarcity:** Lack of irrigation facilities makes crop cultivation challenging.
 
• **Low yields:** Dryland crops often have lower yields compared to irrigated crops.
 
• **Soil erosion:** Wind and water erosion can degrade soil quality in dry regions.
 
 
 
• **Government initiatives:**
 
 
• **National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA):** Aimed at promoting sustainable farming practices in dryland areas.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY):** Focuses on water conservation and efficient irrigation to support dryland farming.
